- When sentiment is consistently negative (last 3–5 days < -0.30), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 7-day average.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling >1.5% from peak), model often fails to adjust; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for 3–5 days post-peak.
- When sentiment is positive but price is falling (e.g., +0.20 sentiment, -0.5% price), model often misreads sentiment; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% relative to prior 5-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast (first 5–7 days); apply 0.5–1.0% downward correction for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., -0.40 → +0.30 → -0.50), model often fails to anticipate; apply 1–2% downward correction for 3–5 days after sentiment flips from positive to negative.
